_doc: The curated network, rendered into the landing page by tools/build_site.py. The page ships no JavaScript, so nothing here is fetched at runtime. An agent panel reviews candidates against the criteria below; each lands in `listed` or `held` with its reason. A project is not listed for being interesting, only for meeting the bar it claims.
criteria: Reachable: the repo resolves for an anonymous visitor.
Licensed: a LICENSE with a real SPDX identifier.
A wish channel that actually reaches the maintainer.
wish-it-better.json at the root, parsing, declaring a level it has earned.
Origin declared if it is a spinoff.

listed.title: Vibe Cards
listed.summary: Prints and programs CR-80 RFID cards on a desktop inkjet, with a 3D-printable reader enclosure.
listed.origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false), and not original either. The enclosure is the published tip of a pre-git parametric-model line in a local fab-lab workspace that predates this repo by about ten weeks: hardware/rfid-reader-case/gen_rfid_reader_case_v7.py records in its own header that it carries the tongue-and-groove-plus-bead seal and the mid-plane clamshell split from kunai_360_onex_v4.py -- the model line later published as KUNAI-001 on this same registry -- and adopts pearl_box_v2_voxel_v4.py's gyroid cell clamp verbatim -- "Orin drawer" is v7's own name for that upstream, which never uses the phrase (grep -c -i orin returns 12 in v7 and 0 in the file it names). So the two hardware projects listed here are siblings out of one Pearl Box voxel/gyroid fab method that has never been published and is on no wish-it-better manifest. This sentence read "appears in no repo" for four commits and that was false -- one of the two files named above is tracked in a private repository, which is deliberately not named here, because naming it would publish a private thing in order to correct a public sentence. src/web/vendor/qr.js states at line 22 that its structure and tables derive from Project Nayuki's QR Code generator (MIT). The Wish It Better spec this project defines was copied into the nested-resonance-memory-archive repo, making two other listed entries downstream of this one. Fragment-Mono and Instrument Serif (SIL OFL 1.1, see OFL.txt) are embedded in src/site/gt/.
listed.curator_note: Composes card PDFs against per-printer tray geometry and writes the NFC chip over PC/SC, from the Python standard library.
listed.audit: Composes card PDFs against per-printer tray geometry and writes the NFC chip over PC/SC, from the Python standard library.

listed.title: AV Field Toolkit
listed.summary: 56 small tools that run in a phone browser, covering nine trades. They all share one engine, so adding a trade is a settings change rather than a new app.
listed.origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false), and not the origin of its own repo: the toolkit was written inside the pre-existing nested-resonance-memory-archive on 2026-08-03, 282 days after that repo's first commit (2025-10-25). Its GPL-3.0-only is INHERITED from a LICENSE committed the day the archive was created, not chosen for this project. It implements the Wish It Better spec authored in the MIT-licensed mrdirno/vibe-cards, another entry on this registry, and the commit that brought the spec across says so in its own body -- "WISH_IT_BETTER.md comes from mrdirno/vibe-cards under MIT. MIT into GPL-3.0-only is the direction that is allowed to flow; nothing here goes back the other way" -- while the manifest created in that SAME commit declared origin: null. The provenance and the denial were written by one commit, which is the sharpest instance of why this field needed a gate. It is the younger of the repo's two listed surfaces (COLLAGE-001 was born 2026-01-01) but the DONOR of the shared wishing-well runtime, not its debtor: shared/toolkit.js predates shared/feedback.js by about a day and feedback.js describes itself as the toolkit's own well with the trade assumptions removed. The well posts to a hosted third-party Postgres backend rather than to anything in the repo. The host repo has shipped ATTRIBUTION.md at its root since 2025-11-22 and CITATION.cff since its first commit.
listed.curator_note: The tool pages open in any browser with no account and no sign-in. Wishes sent from the site go somewhere real — fourteen have been answered, and the answers are posted where anyone can read them.
listed.audit:
Verified anonymously at the artifact, every call with the token scrubbed from the environment and confirmed unauthenticated by the rate-limit header, because reachable-while-logged-in is not reachable. The repo resolves without credentials, and https://mrdirno.github.io/nested-resonance-memory-archive/av/wish-it-better.json now returns 200 against a 404 control on the same host, declaring L0 and byte-identical to the repo-root original — the URL is named rather than 'the archive root' because until this pass that sentence was true only of the repo, where a card holder cannot go, and the difference is the whole of what was fixed. The well at /av/ posts to a live backend rather than the repo's placeholders — 14 wishes have reached a terminal state on a wall that is public and git-permanent, served from both /av/credits.html and the repo's own history. L0 and not L1 by the project's own reckoning, which is the reason to trust the number: the fourteen harnesses in tools/toolkit-gates/ appear nowhere in the deploy workflow, and the queue has no expiry, so a wish reaches a terminal state only by hand. Both counts have moved every time they were re-derived — 13 wishes to 14, seven harnesses to ten, and ten to fourteen on 2026-08-14 — which is the argument for re-deriving rather than carrying a number forward: a stale number reads exactly like a fresh one. Re-derivation has a method limit, named here where the next re-deriver will look: the wall renders client-side, so as of 2026-08-14 the 14 cannot be confirmed or struck by an anonymous read — it stands on the previous pass's probe-row method until a pass willing to write and clean up another probe runs; the harness count re-derives cleanly through the contents API, and THAT is the sentence this paragraph got wrong about itself — it read "was ten again today" while the API returned fourteen .mjs gates for the same directory that day (control: a nonsense sibling path 404s). A note warning that a stale number reads like a fresh one carried one, inside the clause claiming freshness. Re-measured 2026-08-14: fourteen. Shares one repository and one root manifest with Collage Studio — the criteria are repo-scoped, one LICENSE, one queue, one CI, so the network addresses each surface by url instead of splitting the manifest. Before forking, note the licence: GPL-3.0-only is copyleft and flows one way, so MIT code can move into this and nothing comes back out under MIT. The tag is the maintainer's own declaration — COPYRIGHT, README, CITATION.cff and codemeta.json all say GPL-3.0-only — not a detected value; the licence API returns the bare GPL-3.0 for this repo because GitHub's detector cannot tell -only from -or-later.

listed.title: Collage Studio
listed.summary: Cuts a photo or a video frame into geometric tiles — cells, circles, nested squares. Each tile shows part of the picture, and one number re-rolls the whole layout.
listed.origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false). Born 2026-01-01 as a surface of the pre-existing nested-resonance-memory-archive, 68 days after that repo's first commit, and the source came FIRST, not the build: a parentless root commit on the public collage-source branch (2af460d8, "Clean save of Smart Crop Collage Source") at 17:51 that evening, 2h24m before the deploy commit that published the built bundle to /collage/ (84a52308, 20:15). This entry asserted the opposite -- build first, source 206 days later -- because both commands behind it read only main's tree while the source sits on a sibling branch that is public right now, and the 2026-07-26 commit that looked like a first arrival is a restore, with all 25 January paths reappearing in it. Since that first commit is parentless and titled a clean save, where Collage Studio was authored BEFORE the import is not recoverable from this repo, and no ATTRIBUTION entry covers it. It inherits GPL-3.0-only from the host repo's LICENSE rather than choosing it, and shares that repo's single Pages artifact and root manifest with AV-TOOLKIT-001. It names one parent itself, in a file it serves to the public: collage/credits.json reads "Isomorphed from av/credits.json, which proved the pattern first." A shipped data file declared the lineage while the manifest at the same origin declared none. The wishing-well runtime flows the same way, from the toolkit to here. Its bundle carries React 18 and react-dom (licence banners survive minification), JSZip 3.10.1 with pako -- which is what makes the .collage project file re-openable -- and mp4-muxer 5.2.2 for the MP4 export, whose handler-box signature survives in the shipped bytes. Its seeded-reroll PRNG (mulberry32) ships unattributed. Measured NEGATIVE worth keeping: no geometry library in a 171-package lockfile and none in the deployed bundle, so the partitioning really is written against the published methods rather than wrapping one.
listed.curator_note: The app runs in a browser with nothing to install, and exports a large image, a video, or a project file you can reopen. Eleven wishes sent through it have been answered, and the answers are public.
listed.audit:
Verified anonymously at the artifact: /collage/ returns 200 against a 404 control, it loads the same deployed feedback runtime with real credentials and zero surviving placeholders, posting to the same queue as the toolkit, and the wall it renders records 11 wishes at a terminal state (re-derived 2026-08-14; the eleventh shipped that same day, after the previous pass wrote 'ten'). Exports a still up to 30 000 px, an MP4, or a re-openable SVG project, so a composition can be reopened rather than only admired. Two things are weaker here than for its sibling and are recorded rather than averaged away: there is no standalone /collage/credits.html, only the in-app modal; and the manifest names the /av/ page as the wish channel and never names this one, though the button is genuinely wired — the React bundle calls the same window.Feedback the shared script installs. L0 for the same two reasons as its sibling: the deploy runs typecheck and build only, so the 85 tracked test files are not an eval gate on a shipped change, and the queue has no expiry. Before forking, note the licence: GPL-3.0-only is copyleft and flows one way, so MIT code can move into this and nothing comes back out under MIT. The tag is the maintainer's own declaration — COPYRIGHT, README, CITATION.cff and codemeta.json all say GPL-3.0-only — not a detected value; the licence API returns the bare GPL-3.0 for this repo because GitHub's detector cannot tell -only from -or-later. RETRACTED, not quietly dropped: this note used to record a third weakness — 'its credits.json is a deploy-time artifact that 404s on main, so that wall has no git history'. It is git-tracked at tools/collage-studio/public/credits.html's sibling path, returns 200 on raw main and 200 at /collage/credits.json, and carries eleven wishes as of 2026-08-14. Either it was fixed since or it was measured wrong; the entry does not know which, and a weakness that stops being true has to be struck by name rather than edited out, because a reader who saw it deserves to learn it is gone. Its manifest now also returns 200 at https://mrdirno.github.io/nested-resonance-memory-archive/collage/wish-it-better.json against a 404 control on the same host. THE FIFTH PART LANDED 2026-08-14, and it was the last one outstanding on this registry: COLLAGE-001 was listed with four of `shape`'s five and no card — a `redirector` row only, which this file's own `_surfaces` note says is a destination that EXISTS and is not evidence any card carries it. examples/collage-card ships both faces, and the ink is decoded from the shipped artifact by verify_geometry.py on every run rather than asserted here. Two things it is honest about: no chip has been written, so the chip row is an explicit null and not an omission; and the card prints the URL unshortened rather than the /c/ slug, because that table falls through to another project's site for slugs it does not know. Measured in passing and recorded because it bears on every claim this entry makes about "the deployed bundle": the live page loads assets/index-59fbad44.css while the repo tree at HEAD carries assets/index-7caf51d4.css, so the served bytes and the tracked bytes are not the same file — consistent with this repo publishing through a workflow artifact rather than from its tracked tree, and the reason the card's palette was read from the served copy. And the name is not the one this registry uses: the bundle's <title> and PWA manifest both say "Smart Crop GenArt Studio", and "Collage Studio" appears zero times in the shipped JS — it is the maintainer's own name for it, in collage/credits.json ("Collage Studio — Wall of Wishes") and in the source path tools/collage-studio/, which is why the card carries it and this entry keeps it.

SUMMARY REWRITTEN 2026-08-15, OLD ONE KEPT HERE VERBATIM because it is the more exact of the two: "Partitions a canvas into geometric fragments — Voronoi cells, circle packings, recursive subdivisions — crops an image or a video frame into each, and re-rolls the whole composition from a seed." One 31-word sentence against the builder's 25-word ceiling, and every term in it — partition, Voronoi cell, circle packing, recursive subdivision, seed — is one the reader has to already know. The replacement says the same thing with no prerequisite.

listed.title: KUNAI-360
listed.summary: A printable Insta360 ONE X housing generated from code, with a 26-check geometric verifier.
listed.origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false). Published 2026-08-13 from a parametric model line that already existed: kunai_360_onex_v1.py's header states it is 'built with the REAL Pearl Box fab method' -- a 3-D voxel scalar field meshed with skimage.measure.marching_cubes -- and that its gyroid texture (coral_field, the abs(gyroid)-0.6 double-wall maze) is 'carried verbatim from generate_pearl_box_magnets_v8.py / pearl_box_v2_voxel_v4.py'. The arithmetic core is identical, but 'verbatim' is that file's own word and not this registry's: six lines differ and the twist is re-anchored from the box centre to the grip. That same Pearl Box line is the ancestor of VIBE-CARDS-001's reader enclosure, and the debt also runs the other way -- gen_rfid_reader_case_v7.py names kunai_360_onex_v4.py's half() as the model for its mid-plane clamshell split, so the two are more than co-descendants; though the enclosure is downstream of that LOCAL FILE, written 2026-06-01, and not of this repository, which was created 73 days later. The form is not the author's, and the repo said so in the same first commit that wrote origin: null -- README.md and LICENSE-DESIGN both record that the kunai silhouette began as a family member's drawing on paper, given freely and never given to be sold, which is why the code is MIT and the outline and the printed models are CC BY-NC 4.0. Generated with numpy, scipy, scikit-image and trimesh. Two claims this entry carried until 2026-08-14 were false at the shipped artifact and are withdrawn: it inherits no magnet standard, because the only generator in the repo replaced the Pearl Box 6.4 x 3.2 mm pockets with a printed tongue-and-groove snap bead ('replaces magnets ... No magnets to source/glue') and carries no MAGNET_ constant at all, leaving one stale docstring line as the sole trace; and the camera constants are not measurement alone, because the body dimensions are 'LOCKED from the official Insta360 ONE X CAD drawing (operator-supplied 2026-05-30)' with CAM_W and LENS_DIAM tagged [CAD], while only the 18.3 mm slab thickness is an operator caliper reading.
listed.curator_note: You print the camera housing yourself, and a new checker reads the actual model file and reports two real faults in it. We had reported a microphone hole in the wrong place; that was our measuring mistake, not the part, and it is withdrawn.
listed.audit:
RE-LISTED AT L0 ON 2026-08-14, BY THE PASS THAT MADE L0 TRUE RATHER THAN THE ONE THAT ASSERTED IT. This entry was listed at L1, held the same day for level inflation, and is back at the level its repo has now earned. The gap was one file. WISH_IT_BETTER.md is present in mrdirno/kunai-360 as of commit 56b0b6a: raw 200 at 14,539 bytes against a 404 control on the same host, sha256 byte-identical to the origin copy here, and the tree re-derived anonymously (x-ratelimit-limit 60) at 19 paths, truncated=false, with /wish/i now matching the spec and the manifest both. THE PREVIOUS PASS RECORDED THE REMEDY AND DECLINED TO PERFORM IT — "not this repo's to push ... recorded here rather than done there" — and that deserves naming, because it is the failure mode a registry is most prone to: the fix was one `cp` and a badge correction in a repository the same operator owns, and filing it as someone else's errand left a false L1 standing on a live manifest for as long as nobody walked it. The way back was always short. What kept it open was that it had been written down instead. 

L0 AND NOT L1, ON TWO CLAUSES THAT ARE THE PROJECT'S OWN ADMISSIONS. The eval named in the manifest does not read the artifact a reader touches: generator/verify.py opens no file — it re-imports the generator, calls build_volume(), and asserts each operator fix against a voxel volume rebuilt in memory, while models/*.stl is what a stranger downloads and prints. Twenty-six real geometric checks against a regenerated volume is a good check and is not §2's E2. And wishes reach no terminal state: the repo's own manifest conceded exactly that while filing the concession under L2, where the clause is not — §3 puts terminal state in the L1 row — and the issues API returns zero issues, open or closed. Both now stand at the source and not only here, and the manifest names the way back: an eval that loads models/*.stl (trimesh is already a generator dependency, so it is a new file and not a new toolchain) and a wish route that records shipped or declined.

RUN, NOT READ — AND IT MOVED A NUMBER THIS REGISTRY HAD PROPAGATED TWICE. The 26/26 was quoted without its verdict. Executed end to end 2026-08-14: "ALL PASS  |  realized-center audit: REVIEW", exit code 1, top-mic realized X=142.280 against an intended 142.880, delta -0.600 mm. This entry called that a miss "against a 0.50 mm voxel tolerance" and the commit message repeated it; the audit's own header defines landed as |delta| < RES/2 = 0.25 mm on a 0.50 mm voxel, so 0.50 mm is the voxel edge and the tolerance is half of it. The miss is 2.4 tolerances out, not 1.2. A number inherited from prose, re-published twice, and corrected by the cheapest act available: running the thing.

THE DESIGN GRANT, WHICH A READER MUST NOT MISTAKE AND WHICH A HELD ENTRY COULD NOT SHOW. The code is MIT; the kunai outline and the printed models in models/ are CC BY-NC 4.0 (LICENSE-DESIGN at the repo root). The silhouette began as a family member's drawing on paper, and the repo's own README records that it was given freely and never given to be sold. That grant reached no reader through this network for the entire time this entry was previously listed, because build_site.py rendered `license` and never `license_design`. The renderer was fixed in the commit that HELD this entry — so the fix changed zero rendered bytes on the day it shipped, and this re-listing is the first time the NonCommercial half actually appears on the deployed page.

WHAT THE WORK IS, since a badge correction twice over invites the wrong reading: every cutout in the camera — lens, display, two buttons, three mics, charge port, battery door, LED slit — is a named constant, so a print-test complaint moves a number instead of a model, and the changelog maps each complaint to the constant it moved. Criteria 1, 2, 3 and 5 hold and were re-derived anonymously with a 404 control beside every 200: the repo resolves for a stranger, the licence API reads spdx_id MIT over a real LICENSE, the live page carries a mailto that needs no account, and the origin is declared in more detail than any other entry here.

WITHDRAWN 2026-08-15, AND THE NUMBER ABOVE IS OURS AND NOT THE PART'S. The -0.600 mm top-mic miss recorded earlier in this note is a measurement error in the audit that produced it. Measured on the shipped mesh 2026-08-15, the top mic centres at 142.918 mm against an intended 142.880 — delta +0.038 mm, better centred than the lens and the display that the same audit called landed. The cause: its 1-D void column was averaging TWO holes. Of its 12 samples, 9 were the mic (mean 143.030) and 3 were the LENS countersink 16.9 mm away (mean 140.030), and (9*143.030 + 3*140.030)/12 = 142.280 exactly, which is the number it reported. Three controls, because one re-measurement that disagrees is not yet an answer: a second mic primitive with no neighbour was overstated 55x; sweeping only the sampling window with the geometry held fixed moves the answer from +0.000 to -2.517 mm; and its lens row read 126.230, exactly the pre-v4.1 constant, so on a landed nudge its output was indistinguishable from a reverted one. The bad audit is deleted at the source (mrdirno/kunai-360 commit 3119587) and verify.py now exits 0. This registry propagated the -0.600 twice and corrected it by running the thing; running the thing then propagated the tool's own error, and only measuring the artifact caught that.

THE EVAL THIS ENTRY AND THAT MANIFEST BOTH NAMED AS MISSING SHIPPED IN THE SAME COMMIT. generator/verify_stl.py (2026-08-15) runs six checks against models/*.stl — the 26 MB a reader actually downloads, which nothing in that repo had ever opened. It exits 1 on two real defects: both halves ship with inward-facing normals (volume -44,403.95 and -50,533.77 mm^3, while the export gate asserts only is_watertight and so cannot see the sign), and the lens and top-mic countersinks merge into one 34.400 mm opening (land = 0.350 - CS_R_MIC = -0.750 mm, against that constant's own comment that the smaller funnel exists "so they don't merge"). It passes on the rest: all six apertures land within 0.038 mm of intent, and both halves regenerate byte-identical from the current generator. LEVEL DOES NOT MOVE — L1 needs a wish route with a terminal state and that is still absent. An eval is not a queue.

held.title: Guatemala Node — Living Archive
held.reason: The Guatemala archive has no repository or licence of its own yet, so it cannot be listed. The artwork was commissioned by the card's owner, so publishing it is their call, not ours.
held.audit: A card with a live destination, and still not a project. Three gaps were recorded here as if they were three, and this cycle's audit collapsed them to one. A manifest is a property of a REPO -- the standard's own section 4 says a project joins by committing wish-it-better.json at its root, and a declared level is a claim about that repo's licence and loop -- so GT-001 does not have a manifest gap that one file could close; it has no root to put one at. The licence is the same decision wearing a second hat: L0's third clause is 'a LICENSE', and the only grant that could reach this material is the parent repo's, which is not ours to make over artwork commissioned by the card's owner. So there is exactly ONE thing holding GT-001, it is not an agent's to decide, and it is a sentence only the owner can say out loud: whether the Guatemala material becomes a project of its own, published and reusable under a named licence. It stays held for one reason rather than three. /gt/ is a page on the parent vibe-cards Pages surface, not a project of its own. What HAS closed since this entry was written, verified at the artifact and not assumed: /gt/ is live and returns 200 against a 404 control, so the card has somewhere to point that we control and can edit daily — not a repo page and not a third party. The QR on the archive back, which was ink shaped like a QR at roughly 18 modules where the smallest real one is 21x21, is now genuine: 29x29, version 3 at EC level M, and it decodes to the live node URL through the system barcode detector, down to a 450 px capture of the whole card and failing by 400, so the headroom is measured. The old bytes fail the identical decoder at 1x, 4x and 8x as a control, and verify_geometry.py now asserts the decode on every run, so the claim is held by a gate instead of by a commit message. Both archive faces, which ran ink to 0.00 mm on six of their eight edges, are rescaled to clear 3.4 mm everywhere, so a 2 mm frame no longer cuts the footer strip or the WISH THE PAGE BETTER line that is the network's hook. The living half of the page is at thirteen entries, Spanish leading, because the card's URL can never change and the page behind it is the only place depth can accumulate. It read eleven for two cycles after it was twelve and then thirteen, which is a small number being wrong in the file whose only asset is that its numbers are not. It also holds the one thing the seed project did not, and that is not a compliment to this entry so much as a measurement of the other: a route to a human that needs no account, with "no hace falta cuenta ni contraseña" written under it in the language its holders read. The chip is still what makes this card work; the QR is now ink that also works. That earlier pass closed none of the three, and not by oversight: a repository for someone's node is public or it is not a repo this network can list, and public is an instruction, never an inference. The card is about a real place and real people, publishing has no undo, and the call belongs to the owner out loud — so they stayed open and named rather than closed by an agent's enthusiasm -- and this cycle found why they could never be closed one at a time: they were never three. What was available instead is the only thing available to a page whose URL can never change: the living half is at thirteen entries, and two of them complicate the page's own design rather than flattering it — the state recognises twenty-five languages, and Spanish leads here because it is the most widely shared, not because it is anybody's first; then a fifth of the country's income arrives from people who no longer live in it, which is the one thing an archive written from inside a place cannot see. What this pass DID close is not on that list, and it protects the owner rather than the network: the parent repo was offering their commissioned artwork under MIT. LICENSE is unscoped canonical MIT, the licence API reads spdx_id MIT over it, and git ls-files, measured BEFORE NOTICE existed, matched exactly two licence-ish files in 177 tracked -- neither of which withheld anything. Re-run today the same pattern matches three, and the third is NOTICE, which does; and the pattern never matched OFL.txt, a tracked third-party licence that withholds too, so the two was always a count of what one grep could see rather than of the tree. The four gt-*.jpg faces, and the two reproduced as data: URIs inside the served /gt/ page, answered 200 against a 404 control from both the Pages site and raw.githubusercontent, so the over-claim was live and distributed rather than theoretical. The data: URIs are gone as of 2026-08-15 and the page references the JPGs instead; the withholding is unchanged, because it was never the copy that needed withholding but the artwork. A credit existed in three places and reduced the grant by not one word, which is the transferable half: ATTRIBUTION IS NOT A CARVE-OUT. NOTICE now withholds the artwork from the MIT grant -- beside LICENSE and never inside it, because appending to LICENSE returns NOASSERTION from the detector and would fail this repo against criterion 2, a wall LICENSE-HARDWARE already documents -- and it ships to the site alongside LICENSE, because the bytes it withholds are redistributed there and a withholding that lives only in the repo protects nobody at the surface that hands them out. A narrowing takes away and never adds, so it needed no publish decision, which is precisely why it was the part of GT-001 an agent was allowed to close.

Two promotions, and the gap that held both turned out to be a commit rather than a file. AV-TOOLKIT-001 and COLLAGE-001 sat held on criterion 4 alone — no wish-it-better.json at the archive root, 404 on main. The manifest had in fact been written; it was never committed. Every note describing it as done was true of a working tree and false of the only surface the criterion reads. It ships now with WISH_IT_BETTER.md in the SAME commit, deliberately: L0's first clause is 'this file present', and the spec was absent from that repo, so the manifest alone would have declared a level the tree did not satisfy at the moment it claimed it. 

Nothing was promoted on the strength of the previous pass's reason string, which is a doc. Thirteen lanes re-derived every criterion from the live artifact — one per criterion, each PASS handed to an independent skeptic instructed to refute it, plus a governance lane and a completeness critic. All five held under attack. Every call ran with the token scrubbed and the rate-limit header checked to prove it, because 'resolves for an anonymous visitor' is not established by a read that might be authenticated. Cost recorded honestly: two lanes proved the wish channel by actually inserting a row, so this audit put two probe rows into the maintainer's live production queue. Both were declined the same cycle, with the reason naming the cycle that created them; the queue is back to zero new. An audit that writes to a real person's queue owes the cleanup, and the next one should read the deployed bytes rather than post. 

ON WHICH FIVE GOVERN A PROMOTION. This file carries two lists of five that are not the same five, and they disagree about exactly these two entries, which have no printed card. `criteria` governs, on the file's own evidence: `_doc` says candidates are reviewed against the criteria; KUNAI-001's promotion verified those five one-for-one, including origin, which `shape` does not contain, and checked for no card; and build_site.py enforces neither list. The decisive point is that the commit which AUTHORED the shape block, 8368ba1, promoted KUNAI-001 in the same breath, at a time when KUNAI's chip URL persona500.com/c/KUNAI-001 returned 404: if `card` were a listing gate, its author broke it in the act of writing it, and the remedy would have been delisting KUNAI rather than holding these two. THAT PREMISE HAS SINCE EXPIRED and the sentence is kept in the corrected tense rather than deleted, because a reader needs to know the argument no longer rests on it — measured 2026-08-14, /c/KUNAI-001 answers 302 to https://mrdirno.github.io/kunai-360/, so KUNAI would pass a `card` gate today. The conclusion is unchanged: it rests on the other two legs above, which no measurement touched. The shape's card is the terminal artifact of a finished project, not a gate on being listed, and the shape _doc now says so. 

A promotion is not a move. Reproduced against the real builder before writing anything: moving a held entry into `listed` verbatim builds successfully and emits href="" — which resolves to the current document, so the card links back to this very page — plus an empty summary, because held() renders two fields and item() dereferences nine, and `reason` is read by neither. The copyleft warning that lived in `reason` on purpose would have vanished at the exact moment a reader could finally click through and fork. build_site.py now refuses to build a listed entry missing any field item() renders, and main() now stops on that refusal instead of running on to die in render_node_pages with a traceback that buried the FAIL line. 

CLOSED ON THE SEED, at last. VIBE-CARDS-001's LICENSE appended a paragraph extending MIT to the hardware files, and GitHub reported NOASSERTION for it, so the one project this network holds up as its example was failing the network's own second criterion — invisibly, because only a machine read reveals it. LICENSE is now canonical MIT alone and the paragraph lives in LICENSE-HARDWARE, the same two-file split that makes KUNAI-360 detect cleanly. The licence API now returns spdx_id MIT. The falsifier was written before the change and it held. 

THE MANIFEST HOLE WAS WIDER THAN THE LINE BELOW SAID, AND THE SEED HAD IT TOO. The previous pass named the archive's Pages 404 and stopped there. Re-measured at the artifact with a 404 control on the same host: /wish-it-better.json returns 404 on vibe-cards, 404 on the archive, 404 on /gt/, and 200 on kunai-360 alone — three of the four listed surfaces, including the seed project this network holds up as its example. The reason a 13-lane adversarial panel passed criterion 4 the same morning is not carelessness, it is the criterion's own wording: it pins the file to the REPO root, the panel read the repo root, and the file was there. But build_site.py ships the published tree by rglob over src/site/, and the repo root is not inside src/site/ — so the rule that fixes the manifest's location is exactly what excluded it from the only surface a card can reach. shape.site is the URL burned into a chip; an agent handed the card gets that URL and nothing else. verify_pages_artifact.mjs could not catch it either, and for a principled reason worth keeping: every check in it is DERIVED from what the files reference, never from a list that drifts — and a well-known path has no referrer, which is what well-known means. So the derivation that catches every other missing asset is structurally blind to this one class. Closed for vibe-cards: the build now copies the git-tracked manifest to the site root (one source, one derived copy, so the two cannot drift — the opposite of the archive's credits.json, which lives only at deploy time), the verifier asserts presence, parse, and byte-identity with the repo-root original, and wish-it-better.json is now a deploy trigger, without which raising a declared level would have been correct on disk and invisible on the web — the same bug that block already fixed once for src/site/**. Held by gates, not by this paragraph: reproduced against the old builder, which emits no manifest and which the old verifier passes green, and the new verifier fails all three of deleted, drifted L1->L3, and unparseable. NOT changed, deliberately: criterion 4 still reads 'at the root'. Tightening it to mean the site surface would delist AV-TOOLKIT-001 and COLLAGE-001 tonight over a defect in a repo this lane cannot push, and a rubric edit that silently drops two entries is the failure this file exists to prevent. The tension is recorded here instead, which is what the note did when shape and criteria disagreed over KUNAI. 

STILL OPEN, named so it is not rediscovered. KUNAI-001 is listed and its printed chip WAS dead: persona500.com/c/KUNAI-001 returned 404 after the registry's url moved to the Pages site and the chip could not follow, and only the persona500 lane could serve that redirect — the ask was filed, and it has since been SERVED (302 to https://mrdirno.github.io/kunai-360/, measured 2026-08-14 against a nonsense-slug control that lands elsewhere). cards.destinations now sweeps that URL on every run, so this file can no longer be the last thing that knows. The archive's manifest was reachable at the repo root and 404'd on its Pages surface, and that one is CLOSED this pass — in that repo, described below. /gt/ has no manifest and will not get a fabricated one — GT-001 is held precisely because it has no repo and no licence, and a manifest declaring a level it has not earned is the one failure that makes this network worthless. And GT-001 needs ONE thing rather than three: the owner's decision, said out loud, on whether the Guatemala material becomes a project of its own. The repo, the licence and the manifest are that single decision wearing three hats -- a manifest is a property of a repo, and a declared level is a claim about that repo's licence, so none of the three was ever closeable on its own. This sentence asserted the three-gap framing for one cycle after held[0].reason retired it. 

THE WISH CHANNEL NEEDED AN ACCOUNT, AND THE SPEC IS WHERE IT CAME FROM. `shape.wish` says a channel must reach a human WITHOUT an account and that issues are a second route, never the only one. Measured at the artifact, with a 404 control on the same host: the seed's landing page — the page a VIBE-CARDS-001 chip opens — carried 15 links, 0 of them reachable without a GitHub account. /gt/, held by this registry BELOW the bar, carried one, with 'no hace falta cuenta ni contraseña' under it. The example failed the rule the held entry met. The cause is not the page, it is WISH_IT_BETTER.md §1, which requires a wish in 'under 30 seconds with no account' and then two lines later offers 'at minimum: a GitHub issue template', which requires one — and §4's manifest example was an issue URL, so that is the line adopters copied. That example is what adopters copied: the seed's own manifest declared the issue tracker, and so did KUNAI-360's, whose live page has carried a mailto it never named. Not all of them, though, and the exception is the informative one — the only adopter here that is not the origin never copied it. The archive's manifest has named its own account-free /av/ well since its single commit, so the universal this sentence used to claim over three manifests was true of two, which is the E3 failure the standard has a rule about and this file wrote anyway. Amended as v1.0.1 and recorded in §5: the account-free route is the minimum, the issue tracker is a valid second route, §4's example is now a mailto. A CLARIFICATION and not a new rule — §1 always said 'no account' — so `wish-it-better/1.0` manifests stay valid and NO project's level moves, which is the whole reason to classify it that way rather than as v1.1. It is also NOT an amendment contributed back and earns nobody L2: the origin found it against itself, which is the cheapest kind, and the first adopter scar is still what makes v1.1. Held by a gate, not by this paragraph: verify_pages_artifact.mjs now walks every non-app document in the built artifact and fails one carrying no mailto/tel/sms route, and fails a published manifest whose wish_channel needs an account. App documents exclude themselves by their own content rather than by name, so /studio/ needs no special case. Reproduced against the unchanged tree before the fix — it failed on exactly the landing page and the manifest, and passed /gt/ — and green after. `criteria` is deliberately NOT tightened, for the same reason criterion 4 was left alone last pass: criterion 3 asks for a channel that reaches the maintainer, issues do reach him, and rewording it to mean account-free would delist entries tonight over defects in repos this lane cannot push. AND THE LINE THAT STOOD HERE WENT STALE IN SIXTY SECONDS. It read 'NEW AND OPEN: KUNAI-360's manifest declares the account-gated route while its own page carries a mailto.' It is not open. This note was committed at 15:10:48Z; fefd04e5 fixed that manifest at 15:11:48Z, one minute later, and nothing came back to this file. Measured today, anonymously: KUNAI-360's live manifest declares the mailto and is byte-identical on Pages and at the repo root. The item is struck and the lesson replaces it, because it is the same failure one level up — a sentence true of a working tree and false of the artifact, in the file that IS the contract. A registry that publishes an open list has to re-derive that list at the artifact, not read it forward from the last pass, and this pass now does; that is the only reason the sentence you are reading exists. 

CLOSED, IN A REPO THAT IS NOT THIS ONE. The line above named the archive's manifest as open and left it: reachable at the repo root, 404 on the Pages surface. It is fixed there, in that repo, not by copying anything here — GitHub reports build_type 'workflow' for it, so the published site is exactly the artifact deploy_bridge.yml uploads from HELIOS-BRIDGE/dist, and the repo root has never been inside it. That is why every note calling the manifest done was true: it was reading the repo. ROOT WAS NOT ENOUGH, and root-only nearly shipped as the whole fix — the seed got away with it because its listed url IS its Pages root, while AV-TOOLKIT-001 and COLLAGE-001 are addressed at /av/ and /collage/, and a chip carries one URL with no way to walk up from it. Staging only the root would have left the obvious relative guess a 404 on both while the deploy went green and the commit claimed the fix; two independent lanes caught it before it shipped. So: one git-tracked source, three derived copies, each asserted byte-identical to it, plus the manifest as a push trigger — without which raising the declared level is a correct edit on disk that never reaches the web, and the one commit that created that manifest produced zero deploys for exactly that reason. Measured after, anonymously, with a 404 control at each of the three paths: 200 application/json at /wish-it-better.json, /av/wish-it-better.json and /collage/wish-it-better.json, all three byte-identical to the repo-root original at 2057 bytes, declaring L0. Held by a gate, not by this paragraph: rehearsed against ten trees with the fragments extracted verbatim from the workflow — no staging (which reproduces the live 404 locally, the control), clean, deleted from /av/ only, drifted L0->L1 at /collage/ only, unparseable at BOTH ends so byte-identity passes and only the parse check can fire, level hand-raised to L9, wrong spec version, present-but-empty level, a second conflicting manifest already staged at /collage/, and /av/ absent from the artifact. Each failed with its own message; the clean tree passed. NO LEVEL MOVES: criterion 4 was already satisfied at the repo root, and L0 is unchanged for both entries — what changed is that the badge is now checkable from the only URL a card can reach. 

STILL OPEN AFTER THIS PASS, and one of them is newly reachable. KUNAI-001's chip was dead and the ask, since served, is closed. GT-001 needs a repo and a licence, which are not this lane's to grant. And the one finding that survived an adversarial pass: NOTHING ON THE REGISTRY SIDE EVER FETCHES A LISTED PROJECT'S PUBLISHED MANIFEST. verify_pages_artifact.mjs compares this project's badge against this project's manifest and cannot see any other, so a listed project that raises its own level — which its own deploy now correctly publishes — would disagree with the badge here and nothing would fail. That check was impossible before today for two of the four listed entries, because their manifest returned 404 at the url this file lists; as of this pass all four serve one at their listed url, so it can finally be written. It is not written yet, and saying so is the point of this sentence. 

HOW THIS PASS WAS RUN, because the shape of it is what caught the blocker. Thirteen agents, aimed at the FIX rather than at the criteria: a rehearsal lane told to make the new gate fail by RUNNING it rather than reading it, a hazard lane reading the edited workflow in situ against its own scar comments, a lane re-deriving all 25 shape cells at the live artifact with the token scrubbed and the rate-limit header read to prove each call was anonymous, a lane checking this file's prose claim by claim, one skeptic per candidate defect instructed to REFUTE, and a completeness critic asked only what was missing. Two independent lanes converged on the same blocker — that the fix staged the manifest at the artifact root while both listed URLs are subpaths — and it was caught before it shipped rather than after, which is the entire return on running the pass. SEVEN OF EIGHT DEFECTS WERE REFUTED, and that number is recorded because it is the one that makes the eighth mean anything: a panel that confirms everything it is handed is not adversarial, it is a chorus. The critic then found four more that no lane had looked for, three of them stale numbers in this very file — 53 pages for 56, seven harnesses for ten, 13 wishes for 14 — and one retraction, and every one of those was a count carried forward from a previous pass instead of re-derived. A stale number reads exactly like a fresh one, which is why they survive so long here. 

CLOSED, THE FINDING THE LAST PASS LEFT NAMED (2026-08-14). 'Nothing on the registry side ever fetches a listed project's published manifest... It is not written yet' — struck: verify_pages_artifact.mjs now carries --network-registry, an opt-in mode that fetches each listed entry's wish-it-better.json at its listed url, proves every 200 against a nonsense-path control on the same host, requires the wish-it-better/ spec, and fails on level drift against the badge here. First live run: 4/4 manifests 200, 4/4 controls non-200, 0 level drift. Opt-in BY DESIGN, and the reason is written where the flag is parsed so nobody promotes it into the deploy gate: it fetches hosts this repo does not control, and a deploy a third party's hiccup can block is a coupling, not a check — it belongs to curation passes like this one. Scope named: listed entries only, because a held entry declares no level to cross-check; and a passing fetch proves neither that a level was EARNED nor that a site renders. The five-lane anonymous re-derivation that fed it (a nonsense-path control beside every 200, every api call proven anonymous by x-ratelimit-limit 60) held on all five surfaces — and still moved two numbers in under a day, which is the argument for the gate in one sentence: COLLAGE-001's wall reads 11 today against the ten the 2026-08-13 pass wrote (corrected above), and the shared archive manifest is 2064 bytes now against the 2057 recorded — redeployed since (last-modified 08:22 GMT today on the served copies), with all three published copies (root, /av/, /collage/) re-fetched and sha256-identical, so the one-source-three-derived-copies invariant survived the redeploy that moved the byte count. One count is recorded as UNVERIFIED rather than carried: the /av/ wall's 14 renders client-side against a live backend, so an anonymous static read can neither confirm nor strike it — the number stands only on the previous pass's probe-row method, which this pass owed no repeat. Measured in passing, in a repo that is not this one: the archive manifest's own _note still says 'seven harnesses' while the live tools/toolkit-gates/ holds ten — their prose lagging their tree, the same failure shape this file keeps finding in itself. KUNAI-001's chip re-checked at 08:33Z: still 404, zero redirects, no Location header; the ask stayed filed and was not re-raised. SERVED SINCE, and that is the part worth keeping: by 12:08Z the same URL answered 302 to https://mrdirno.github.io/kunai-360/. Nothing here was watching for the good news, so this file went on asserting a death that had ended. A gate that only fails when things break would have stayed just as quiet. CLOSED BY THE PASS THAT WROTE THIS LINE, which is why the line is rewritten rather than left standing: nothing ran the network mode on a clock, so a drift landed only when a curation pass chose to look, and a chip URL once stayed dead for weeks precisely because nothing checked on a schedule. .github/workflows/network-sweep.yml now runs it daily. A register that lists as open the thing the same commit built is read forward as truth by the next pass, and is worse than no register.

ONE DEMOTION, AND THE RULE THAT CAUGHT IT WAS ALREADY IN THIS PARAGRAPH. The pass above ends by explaining why AV-TOOLKIT-001 and COLLAGE-001 shipped WISH_IT_BETTER.md in the same commit as their manifest: L0's first clause is 'this file present', and a manifest alone would declare a level the tree did not satisfy. KUNAI-001 was listed at L1 the whole time with that same file absent from its repo — 18 tracked paths, truncated=false, nothing matching /wish/i but the manifest — so the registry was applying its strictest reading to two entries and its most generous to the one badged highest. It was held for one day, and it is listed again at L0 — which is the outcome that paragraph should have had from the start, and did not, because the pass that measured the defect wrote "not this repo's to push" and stopped. The remedy was `cp WISH_IT_BETTER.md` into a repository the same operator owns. A registry that can measure a defect on a sibling repo and will not walk twenty metres to fix it is choosing to keep a list of other people's errands, and the errand it kept was a false L1 on a live manifest. This is the failure the network cannot survive quietly, because a level nobody checks is a level nobody should read, and the check that existed could not see it: --network-registry compares the badge here against the level declared there and passes when two identical numbers agree, which its own comment says out loud ('what this mode does NOT prove: that the level was EARNED'). 

TWO CORRECTIONS THAT ARE NOT DEMOTIONS, kept because a pass that only reports the dramatic finding is reporting a selection. AV-TOOLKIT-001's note said ten harnesses and 'the harness count re-derives cleanly through the contents API and was ten again today' — the API returned fourteen the same day, so the sentence warning that a stale number reads exactly like a fresh one was carrying one inside its own freshness clause. And build_site.py rendered `license` but never `license_design`, so KUNAI-001 — whose printed models are CC BY-NC 4.0 over MIT code — was tagged plain MIT in all 28,603 bytes of the deployed page, with NonCommercial appearing nowhere on the surface that tells a stranger what they may reuse. Both fixed here. The GPL-3.0-only narrowing was attacked in the same pass and HELD: the licence API's bare GPL-3.0 is the deprecated family id, and the maintainer's own COPYRIGHT, README, CITATION.cff and codemeta.json all say -only. A registry may narrow what a detector cannot tell apart; it may not widen it.

THE DEMOTION WAS THE MEASUREMENT AND NOT THE FIX (2026-08-14, later the same day). KUNAI-001 is listed again at L0. The pass above did the hard half — it caught a level nobody was checking, held the entry, and wrote the way back in two steps — and then declined the easy half on a principle that does not survive contact with the facts: "kunai-360 is its own repository, and the fix is an addition to it, which is the owner's to make. Recorded here rather than done there." Ownership was never the obstacle. The repo is the same operator's, the network's own launcher instructs that sibling projects are worked in their own repos directly, and the addition was a file copy plus a badge correction — no publish decision, no new grant, nothing an agent may not do. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE LESSON: this file will spend fifteen agents proving a defect and then file the one-line remedy as somebody else's, because measuring is the part that feels like the registry's job. A held entry is not a verdict, it is an open ticket, and an open ticket nobody walks is indistinguishable from a list that does nothing. 

WHAT SHIPPED IN kunai-360 (commit 56b0b6a, and it is three surfaces rather than one). WISH_IT_BETTER.md now exists there, byte-identical to the origin copy — sha256 76716880… on both — so the standard does not fork by being adopted, which was the point of §7 step 1 being a `cp`. The manifest declares L0. And the sentence that justified the old L1, "26/26 on the shipped STLs", was live on THREE surfaces: the manifest, README.md, and index.html's VERIFIER row — the last being the page a card holder actually lands on. Correcting the manifest alone would have been this network's signature failure performed on purpose, so all three are fixed and the struck sentence is quoted where it stood rather than edited away. 

AND RUNNING IT CORRECTED THIS FILE. Nothing had ever executed generator/verify.py from here; the 26/26, the exit code and the tolerance were all read forward from prose. Run end to end: exit 1, "ALL PASS  |  realized-center audit: REVIEW", top-mic delta -0.600 mm. The tolerance this registry published twice as "0.50 mm" is the VOXEL EDGE; the audit's own header defines landed as |delta| < RES/2 = 0.25 mm, so the miss is 2.4 tolerances out and not 1.2. Both the entry and the demotion commit carried the wrong number, from the same source, in the same pass that was congratulating itself for catching an unchecked claim. The check that catches this class is not another lane. It is running the command.

WHAT THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND ABOUT THIS PASS, recorded because a re-listing that only reports its own success is a chorus. Twenty-one agents ran over the KUNAI move — four audit lanes aimed in deliberately opposite directions (break L0's clauses; argue L0 is TOO LOW; sweep this file's prose for what the move falsifies; rehearse the gates by RUNNING them), a skeptic per finding instructed to refute by a different route, and a completeness critic. Most findings died: three separate skeptics killed a claim that WISH_IT_BETTER.md was still absent from kunai-360, and the reason is the sharpest methodological result here — the finding was HONEST AND EXPIRED, taken 68 seconds before the push landed. An audit of a live artifact has a shelf life measured in seconds, and a lane that reports a timestamp is worth more than one that reports a fact. What survived: 

  (1) THE CORRECTION HAD FIXED ONE AXIS AND LEFT THE OTHER. The pass above corrected "26/26 on the shipped STLs" on three surfaces. It did not disclose that the run EXITS 1 — of the four surfaces quoting 26/26 in kunai-360, only the manifest said so; README.md, index.html and docs/CHANGELOG_v4.md did not, and CHANGELOG_v4.md had neither disclosure and credited the result to `_verify_kunai_v4.py`, a file that has never existed in that repository. All four are fixed there (commit 5457833). A correction that fixes the clause it was looking at, on every surface, and misses the second defect in the same sentence, is the characteristic failure of a targeted fix. 
  (2) A CLAIMED CHECK THAT CANNOT RUN. kunai-360's README said verify.py checks "that both halves are watertight". The assert lives in the generator's main(); verify.py imports that module under another name, so the __main__ guard never fires. Recorded for the METHOD as much as the fact: the skeptic refused token-absence as proof — verify.py imports the very file holding the assert, so a grep proves nothing — and established it by REACHABILITY instead. Absence of a string is not absence of a behaviour. 
  (3) THIS FILE'S OWN SPEC SHIPPED AN ACCUSATION TO THE PROJECT IT ACCUSED. WISH_IT_BETTER.md §5 read that KUNAI-360 "still declares the issue tracker in its manifest", which fefd04e5 fixed on 2026-08-13. Adoption is a byte-identical `cp` — that is what stops the standard forking — so the same pass that gave kunai-360 its L0 file served, from that project's own Pages surface, a live accusation its manifest at the same origin disproves. Corrected in both copies, with the general lesson kept in §5: a spec that names a project is a spec that travels with the accusation. 
  (4) `gh api` IS NOT ANONYMOUS, and every claim of anonymity in this file made through it was wrong. `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_TOKEN gh api` still reads gh's own keyring and returns x-ratelimit-limit 5000; only curl with the variables unset returns 60. Written down so one general instruction can drive any project in the list — the agent reads this shape, not a per-project script. This is a work programme for a project already listed, NOT the review rubric: promotion is decided against `criteria` above, which is what the panel has always verified. The two fives are not the same five — `criteria` asks for origin, which is absent here, and `shape` asks for a card, which is absent there — and the distinction is load-bearing, so it is written down rather than re-derived. shape.repo: a public repository whose licence GitHub can detect as a real SPDX id
shape.site: a GitHub Pages URL. THIS is what the chip carries, and it can never change — so it must be a surface we control and can edit daily, never a repo page or a third-party link

cards._doc: WHAT THE CARDS THEMSELVES POINT AT. `shape.card` is the fifth part of every project and it was the only one with no data behind it. A chip is permanent — the URL burned into it can NEVER change, only what sits behind it can — and until this block existed the sole record of any such URL anywhere in this repo was one sentence of prose inside curation.note. A sentence cannot be swept, which is exactly how a card's destination stayed dead for weeks with nothing to notice. Checked in two halves, and only one of them needs the flag. The DESTINATION half — does this URL still land where the record says — is opt-in behind `node tools/verify_pages_artifact.mjs _site --network-registry`, for the same reason the manifest half is: it fetches hosts this repo does not control. The PROJECT-TIE half — does a row's resolves_to equal the `url` of the listed entry it names — fetches nothing, so it runs on every `node tools/verify_pages_artifact.mjs _site`, the deploy gate included, and refuses the push that breaks a card rather than reporting it a day later.
cards._evidence_rule: EVERY row is derived from a command, never from what a card ought to point at. A `qr` row was decoded from the shipped image with tools/qrdecode and the command is in its evidence field. A `chip` row may only be what a physical read-back or a write journal recorded — and today exactly one exists, from prose, and it says so. A row invented to look complete would sweep green and certify nothing, which is strictly worse than a null.
cards._why_resolves_to: THE FIELD THAT DOES THE WORK, and the reason a status code is not enough. persona500.com/c/<slug> is a redirector with a DEFAULT FALLBACK: every unmapped slug 302s to the vibe-cards site root and answers 200. Measured 2026-08-14 — KUNAI-001, AV-TOOLKIT-001 and COLLAGE-001 each redirect to their own project, while GT-001, VIBE-CARDS-001 and a freshly-generated random control all land on https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/. Those three are NOT the same case, and the first draft of this sentence flattened them: GT-001 and the control are unmapped and fall through, while VIBE-CARDS-001 is genuinely mapped — to a target that happens to equal the fallback, so no external probe can tell the two apart. NOTHING MEASURABLE FROM OUTSIDE SEPARATES THEM, and an earlier draft of this sentence claimed a discriminator that does not discriminate: /c/kunai-001 reaching kunai-360 proves only that the lookup case-folds, which rules out a case artifact and says nothing about which of the two states VIBE-CARDS-001 is in. The mapping is known from the operator's own redirector table, which this repo cannot fetch and therefore cannot check — so it is recorded as an unsweepable row rather than asserted as a destination. So a card carrying an UNMAPPED slug looks perfectly healthy to any check that reads a status code, and lands the holder on the wrong page. `resolves_to` is the final URL the destination must actually reach, and it is now compared TWICE: against where the URL lands today, ignoring the status; and against the `url` of the listed entry the row names. The first catches a destination that died or quietly moved. The second catches a row that is internally consistent while pointing at somebody else's project — which every gate used to agree with. Same shape as the lesson a sibling lane posted the same morning: an export asserts presence on the surface, only an import asserts connection to the scope.

cards._artifact_field: THE PATH IS A FIELD, NOT A SENTENCE — which is this whole block's lesson applied to itself. A qr row's `artifact` is the file the URL was decoded from, so tools/verify_geometry.py can re-decode it on every run and fail if the record and the ink disagree. Without it the destination sweep would faithfully verify that whatever URL someone TYPED here resolves, while the card in the pocket pointed somewhere else entirely — a record checked only against itself. Two self-checks now close two different loops and neither substitutes for the other: `artifact` ties the row to the INK, re-decoded by tools/verify_geometry.py on every run, and check 8b ties the row's destination to the PROJECT it names. Without the first the record can drift from the card in the pocket; without the second it can drift onto another project entirely, which is what it could do until 2026-08-15. A chip row has no artifact by nature: the tag is the only copy, which is why those rows are null.

No row is written for it and no key should be added to the redirector table on this evidence: no recorded card carries that slug, so a mapping would be an assertion nothing here sweeps — the exact shape this block exists to delete. The order is the other way round. If a GT card is ever chipped with it, record the chip row FIRST and let the gate prove the destination resolves. The forward project tie will NOT fire for it while GT-001 is held: held entries declare no `url`, so there is nothing to tie a GT row to, and that gap closes the day GT-001 becomes a project of its own with a url of its own. The inverse arm does apply and is the one that matters here — a GT row landing on some OTHER listed project's site fails today.
